correctness.rationale: For every q≥0 the killed generator is a positive symmetric Dirichlet operator A_q minus the spatially skew propulsion vB. Factoring A_q^{-1/2} gives an everywhere bounded real skew-adjoint K_q and the exact quadratic resolvent identity. Its positive spectral measure has no atom at zero because the directional derivative B has trivial kernel on spatial Dirichlet functions (one-dimensional line-section trace argument). The spectral theorem proves all derivative signs, strictness, high-speed limit, and first-passage Laplace order; Cauchy–Schwarz proves reciprocal concavity and Jensen gives the global rational bound. Finite diagnostic assertions passed (415); they support, but do not replace, these analytic steps.

value.rationale: The quantitative question of whether increasing swimmer speed globally improves survival is motivated by pointwise counter-behavior in absorbing active-particle escape. The theorem gives nonlocal, shape-independent, all-speed Laplace-transform ordering for every exponential mortality/discount parameter and a strictly completely monotone shape hierarchy, not simply a small-v Taylor term. It also transfers a measurable weak-swimming susceptibility into a global rational lower bound. These are genuine sharp structural constraints for a natural kinetic model; the proof uses classical functional calculus but its evaluated first-passage content exceeds the previously available passive-versus-active bound.
